software.backgroundActivity: F-Droid lists run-at-startup permission for 3.4.3; no general background-use measurement published
software.battery: Unknown; authenticator code generation is local.
software.description: Open-source Android authenticator with encrypted local vaults and export support.

evidence.claim: Aegis documents an encrypted local vault and user-controlled backup/export behavior.
F-Droid lists Aegis 3.4.3 (82) as requiring Android 6.0+, supporting arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86 and x86_64, with a 6.6 MiB APK.

software.internetRequirement: Not required for local OTP generation; network may be used by user-selected backup/export workflows
limitations: User is responsible for securely backing up exported vaults
software.name: Aegis Authenticator
software.networkActivity: Core OTP generation is local; backup/export destination behavior depends on user choices

privacyDetails.collected: No account is required for local use; the checked project documentation describes a local encrypted vault rather than a hosted account service.
privacyDetails.controls: Vault encryption, password/biometric unlock, and user-controlled export/backup options are documented.
privacyDetails.deletion: Local app data and exported backup copies must be managed separately by the user.
privacyDetails.encryption: Project documentation describes AES-256-GCM vault encryption with password-derived and Android Keystore-supported unlocking.
privacyDetails.practicalImplications: Aegis can operate as a local-only authenticator, but the privacy of exported backups depends on where the user stores them. Plaintext exports expose OTP secrets.
privacyDetails.purpose: Local storage and generation of OTP credentials; optional exports/backups are user-directed.
privacyDetails.recipients: No routine remote recipient is documented for local vault use; external backup/storage providers chosen by the user are separate recipients.
privacyDetails.sharing: User-initiated export or backup can share vault data with the selected destination.

software.privacySummary: The app is open source and keeps its vault locally unless the user exports or backs it up through another system.
